q1_issues.issue: 'transmitted by ticks' is a participial post-modifier, i.e. a reduced relative ('an infection that is transmitted by ticks'), which the instruction set requires be reified as an event with the by-phrase taking the active subject's Agent role, and explicitly forbids rendering as a relation named after the participle; the kind-relation route used here also fails that construction's own trigger, since the modified head 'an infection' is an indefinite singular rather than a bare kind NP.

'Lyme disease' is fused into one compound-kind symbol with a genus atom, but the casing rule makes the capitalized run 'Lyme' the name (its own symbol plus a mandatory Name fact) with the adjacent lowercase common noun stated in a separate kind atom, and Compound concepts is explicitly barred for proper nouns; no Name atom is emitted on either reading.

q2_gaps: a proper name that denotes a KIND rather than an individual ('Lyme disease', 'Down syndrome'): Names and casing assumes an entity referent and mandates a Name fact, while Compound concepts is explicitly barred for proper nouns, so which route a named kind takes is unspecified
notes: Transmit is a licensed head shape under the open-class kind-relation license, so the defect there is the routing rather than the vocabulary. If the compound-kind route were the intended one, 'Lyme' is a noun modifier and correctly gets no genus, leaving the missing Name atom as the only casing-side issue.
